1.explanation: • full-page-screenshot.js: this gatherer produces the full-page screenshot artifact (fpss) that we need as the single source image to crop our thumbnails from instead of hot-linking. • unsized-images.js: this is the audit that flags tags missing width/height and currently hands off the raw URLs to the thumbnails renderer. • screenshot-thumbnails.js: this audit builds the thumbnail entries today – it’s where we must swap out the remote URLs and inject our base64-cropped images from the fpss artifact. • element-screenshot-renderer.js: the report’s HTML/JS template that takes each thumbnail URL and emits the tag – by pairing it with the new data URIs we ensure the report embeds the images locally. • report-assets.js: when building the standalone HTML report we bundle or inline assets; this file must be aware of the new embedded thumbnails so that it doesn’t try to copy external images. • devtools-report-assets.js: similar to report-assets.js, but for the Chrome DevTools Panel – it gathers and bundles report assets; it needs to pick up the new base64 thumbnails rather than slicing in external references.
1.bug_scenario: When the “Image elements do not have explicit width and height” audit (unsized-images) runs, Lighthouse currently generates a series of small tags in the report that hot-link back to the remote site for each thumbnail. This not only leaks external requests (breaking CSP/mixed-content on HTTPS), but also forces the report viewer to pull in external assets. The goal is to switch from hot-linking each image URL to embedding locally-generated, data-URI thumbnails cropped out of the single full-page screenshot (fpss) that Lighthouse already captures. That way no remote requests are made and the report is self-contained.

2.explanation: • gather/gatherers/image-elements.js and gather/gatherers/full-page-screenshot.js collect the raw `` bounding boxes and the full-page screenshot artifact. • computed/image-records.js turns those DOM captures into a uniform record list. • audits/screenshot-thumbnails.js uses the records and fpss to build thumbnail data (currently it hot-links to record.src for some detail types). • audits/image-size-responsive.js (the audit that flags missing width/height) assembles the detail items and plugs in the snippet/src that ends up hot-linking. • report/renderer/details-renderer.js reads any column of type=thumbnail and invokes the thumbnail logic to emit an `` tag. • report/renderer/element-screenshot-renderer.js formats the screenshot-derived image for a data URI. • clients/extension/devtools-entry.js and devtools-report-assets.js bundle and register the report-renderer in the DevTools panel, so changes in rendering flow through to the UI. • report/generator/report-assets.js in the HTML-report generator is responsible for inlining or copying assets; it too must be updated to allow embedding the new data-URI thumbnails in standalone reports. All these files form the pipeline that currently ends up hot-linking the remote `src` and must be updated to crop from the fpss, convert to base64, and embed locally instead.
2.bug_scenario: When running the Lighthouse audit “Image elements do not have explicit width and height” in DevTools, the report currently displays a tiny `` thumbnail for each offending `` that simply hot-links back to the site’s original `src`. On an HTTPS report this breaks CSP/mixed-content rules and leaks remote requests. The goal is to extract each failing image’s bounding box from the full-page screenshot (fpss), resize it to a thumbnail, and embed it as a `data:image/...` URI so no external requests are made.
